physical_interpretation: In 133Ba Tables 1 and 2, Rojeeta Devi et al. 2021 report exceptionally large interband B(E2)out / B(E2)in ratios of 2.94(18), 2.36(20), and 3.40(22), which are substantially higher than typical wobbling values (~0.2-0.3 in Lu isotopes). Our algebraic deconstruction reveals how this arises from the (E_in / E_out)^5 kinematic factor: 1. For 743.4 keV (in-band 810.8 keV), (E_in/E_out)^5 is 1.54, which together with lambda = 2.35 and f_E2 = 81.5% gives 2.95; 2. For 812.0 keV (in-band 958.3 keV), (E_in/E_out)^5 is 2.29, which together with lambda = 1.30 and f_E2 = 79.2% gives 2.36; 3. For 457.6 keV (in-band 641.9 keV), (E_in/E_out)^5 reaches a massive 5.42! Even though the intensity ratio lambda is only 0.80, the energy factor of 5.42 times f_E2 = 78.3% blows up the extracted B(E2)out/B(E2)in to 3.40. This provides an essential Day 18 demonstration of the extreme sensitivity of E2 transition probability extraction to the fifth power of energy: small differences between interband and in-band transition energies create enormous amplification factors in relative B(E2) values, which must not be confused with unphysically large quadrupole transition operators.
